# Create-Bead

## Overview

This skill turns an ask into filed beads. It is the only authoring path: the always-loaded rules (the repo's `AGENTS.md`) carry only the invariants.

**One ask, one bead.** The operator states an ask once; it lands as one coherent change. A bead cuts across every layer the ask needs — backend, frontend, tests, docs — because a worker split from its other half loses the context that makes the pieces fit. The bead splits only at a real boundary (One bead per ask, below). There is no cap on acceptance lines or description words, and no target bead count.

**Product level, never the steps.** A bead says what is wanted and how we will know it worked. It never tells the worker how to build it: a spec that prescribes implementation passes its mistakes downstream, and the worker reading the repo knows the code better than the author guessing at it.

**One transaction per filing.** Every gate-approved bead is a node in one `bd create --graph <plan.json>` call — a lone bead is a one-node plan, and its parent and blockers ride the same plan. bd applies a plan in one transaction, so a bead never exists without its blocker edges: a loaded workshop drains a bead the moment it is ready.

**Quality by construction.** Before filing, the skill runs `/ac-quality-review` on each draft's acceptance criteria and tightens what it flags, inside a 2-attempt budget (Internal AC-quality gate, below). No step after the claim re-checks acceptance quality (work contract §2).

## Invocation modes

### Args mode (programmatic)

The invoker passes one of two inputs.

**A bead spec.** Required keys: `title`, `type`, `priority`, `description`, `acceptance`, `touches`. Optional: `key`, `parent`, `design`, `notes`, `labels`, `blocked_by`, `ac_labels`, `short_name`, `agent`, `crucible`.

- `key` — the node's plan-local key (default `bead`).
- `parent` — an EXISTING bead id; becomes the node's `parent_id`.
- `blocked_by` — EXISTING bead ids this bead waits on; each becomes an edge `{"from_key": <key>, "to_id": <id>, "type": "blocks"}`.
- `ac_labels` — one short label per non-blank `acceptance` line, in order. Absent, the skill authors them (`ac_labels` below).
- `short_name` — the bead's name in narrow columns. Absent, the skill authors it from the title (`short_name` below).

```yaml
title: "Expired sessions sign the user out cleanly"
type: feature
priority: 2
parent: djinn-auth1
blocked_by: ["djinn-abc12"]
description: |
  **What is wanted:** a user whose session expires mid-task is signed out with their place kept...
acceptance: |
  Given an expired token on any protected route → 401 with error code session_expired
  Given a 401 session_expired in the app → the sign-in page opens with the user's unsaved draft still in the editor after sign-in
design: "Tokens are issued in internal/auth/; the app's request layer is web/src/lib/api/."
notes: "Source: docs/auth-design.md §Expiry"
labels: "auth"
touches: ["internal/auth/", "web/src/lib/api/"]
ac_labels: ["401 on an expired session", "Draft kept across sign-in"]   # optional; authored when absent
short_name: "Clean session expiry"   # optional; authored from the title when absent
agent: "codex gpt-6-astra high"   # optional; see `agent` below
# crucible: {...}                 # only on a formula:crucible bead; see `crucible` below
```

A payload missing a required key returns a structured error naming the missing keys; never invent a title, priority, type or path list.

**An ask.** `ask:` — the operator's words, verbatim — plus any of `parent`, `priority`, `labels`, `blocked_by`, `agent`. The skill reads the repo, drafts the nodes the ask needs (usually one), and gates each.

Either way, without `--execute` the skill files nothing and returns the gate-approved plan (Output); with `--execute` it files it.

### Interactive mode (bare invocation)

Ask only what the ask and the repo leave open, in this order:

1. **Title** — a plain descriptive phrase naming the change the operator would notice. Beside it, show the `short_name` you authored, for the operator to correct.
2. **Type** — `epic` / `feature` / `task` / `chore` / `bug`.
3. **Priority** — P0-P4, as urgency (0=critical, 4=backlog).
4. **Parent** — bead id, or `none`.
5. **Blocked by** — existing bead ids this bead waits on, or `none`.
6. **The ask** — what is wanted, why, and the goal beyond it.
7. **Constraints and exclusions** — what must stay true, and what is out.
8. **Done** — how we will know it worked. Draft `acceptance_criteria` from this and show the `ac_labels` you authored beside it, one per line.
9. **Design hints** *(optional)* — binding constraints and where things live.
10. **Touches** — the paths this bead will change. Derive the default from the repo and the answer to 9 and offer it back rather than asking cold; directories when unsure.
11. **Source / context** *(optional)* — plan reference, sibling beads.
12. **Agent** *(optional, operator's call)* — ask only when the operator named who should do the work. See `agent` below.

When the ask is to move a number rather than reach a done-state, run the crucible interview (`crucible` below) instead of questions 8-10.

Draft each field, settle every hidden-feature line with the author (Hidden features, below), run the gate, show the assembled plan for confirmation, then file it.

## Preflight — bd 1.3.0 floor

Before drafting, run `bd --version`. Below **1.3.0**, `bd create --graph` does not carry every bead field — `acceptance_criteria`, `design`, `notes`, `labels` and `metadata` are lost. **Stop before any filing** with an error naming both versions: `bd <installed> is below the 1.3.0 floor bd create --graph needs; upgrade bd and retry.` Do not fall back to one-at-a-time `bd create`.

## Writing the bead

Read the code, docs and `DECISIONS.md` rulings the ask touches before drafting, so the bead names what exists and binds to what is settled. Then write each field under its own key — never concatenate fields:

| Field | Holds |
|---|---|
| `description` | **What is wanted** — the change, in the operator's terms. **Why** — the problem it solves. **The goal beyond the goal** — what the operator is really after, so the worker can make the calls the bead does not. **Constraints** — what must stay true (a compatibility promise, a performance floor, an interface others read). **Exclusions** — what is out, named. |
| `acceptance_criteria` | How we will know it worked: observable outcomes, one per line (Acceptance criteria, below). |
| `design` | Binding constraints and pointers to where things live: the files, rulings and docs that bear on the work. Never a numbered step list, a prescribed order or a file-by-file plan — unless order is itself the requirement. A build order the operator only suggests ("I'd start by…, then…") is not a requirement: leave it out of every field, not even marked as a leaning. |
| `notes` | Source and context: where the ask came from (`Source: <file path> §<section>`, or the operator and the date), sibling beads, an operator go. |
| `metadata` | `touches`, `ac_labels`, `short_name`, and `agent` or `crucible` when set — each below. Read by the harness and the ops room, not by the worker. |

Every constraint and every exclusion the ask names appears in the description; each one a reviewer can check also gets its own acceptance line. When the ask names deliverables by name (files, endpoints, commands, screens), each appears in an acceptance line or the description says why it is out — absorbed into prose, it gets dropped.

The description is a brief, not a build instruction: "a user whose session expires mid-task should lose nothing" lets the worker build depth; "add a 401 handler to api.ts" gets exactly that handler. Use markdown structure (bolded labels, bullets) when the content is long enough to benefit. Prefer a pointer to a committed doc (`Read docs/support-workspace.md §3.3`) over pasting its prose: inline text is paid by every agent that loads the bead.

A child of an epic carries its own delta; the shared brief lives once in the epic's `description`, and a `notes` line names it: `Context: parent epic <id> carries the shared brief.` The worker reads the parent before coding (work contract §2). A standalone bead carries its whole intent inline.

Priority is urgency, project-wide: the follow-up floor, the reaper and triage all read it that way. Never encode order as priority; order is edges.

Labels are free-form, 2-4 per bead, for filtering. Stamp **no `formula:*` label** by default: the default `iter` formula reviews every bead the same way. `formula:claude` (implement on Claude when codex is unavailable) and `formula:codex` (every agent step on codex) select a provider and are the operator's call, stamped only when asked for by name. `formula:crucible` changes what the bead is (`crucible` below).

## Acceptance criteria

**One criterion per line.** No semicolons separating criteria, no paragraph prose, no markdown bullets. Each non-blank line is one independently checkable outcome; blank lines may group lines and do not count. Every downstream reader counts lines: the harness writes one evidence row per non-blank line (work contract §6), and `/verify-acceptance` checks each.

**An outcome, never a step.** Each line says what is true when the work is done, in terms a reviewer can check by running, using or reading the result: what the user sees and can do, what a command prints, what an endpoint returns, what no longer exists. It names no technology, library, file layout or function unless that name is itself the requirement (a public command, an endpoint others call, a file another tool reads). An observable behaviour is its own verification surface: the line needs no test name or file:line.

**Every number names where it is measured.** A threshold ("under 5 s", "500 rows", "at most 28 cells") names the test, fixture, command or "verified by dogfooding" step that checks it. Prefer a structural fact when the number cannot be tested: "imposes no cap on criterion count" beats "handles a dozen criteria".

**State the precondition when it changes the meaning.** Use the compact form `Given X → Y` on one line: "Shows an error message" admits one hard-coded banner; "Given a 5xx from the tickets API → the list shows a retry banner with the error code" does not. Never split a `Given` onto its own line, and skip the form where plain prose already states the precondition ("Returns 401 for expired tokens").

**No abstract nouns.** "Works well", "idempotence contract", "well-defined behaviour", "scales well" each admit any implementation. Name the operation, the equivalence and the scope: "Render(Render(F)) is byte-identical to Render(F) for every step".

**Fit the lines to the ask.** A technical ask — an API, infrastructure, a developer tool, a refactor — takes structural lines ("POST /api/tokens returns 201 with {token, expires_at}", "no reference to `old_column` remains under `internal/`") and carries no empty, loading or error-state, keyboard or other UI line. An ask with a user interface gets a line for each action the user takes and its result ("hovering a bar shows its period and revenue", "Enter opens the selected ticket") and one for the data volume it must stay usable at. The work contract §4 visual rules (empty, loading and error states, keyboard reach, readable at 3x volume, tooltips that wrap) are already implicit criteria for every visual change: add a line only where the ask fixes something specific, such as what an empty list says. Named visual patterns to omit are exclusion lines (`No pill-shaped buttons`), never "avoid a generic look".

**Test assertions are not outcomes.** "100% branch coverage" or "component renders with props" describe the build; write what the test would prove. A test-suite line belongs only on an ask about the tests themselves, or as one line that the repo's gate passes.

**Before (prescribes the build):**

> - Add `RevenueChart.svelte` using d3-scale with an SVG `<g>` per bar
> - X-axis via `d3.axisBottom`, y-axis via `d3.axisLeft`

**After (what the user sees and can do):**

> - The revenue view shows one bar per month for the last 20 months, ranked by revenue, with month and revenue labels readable at 20 bars
> - Hovering a bar shows its month, revenue, order count and change on the year before
> - Clicking a bar filters the orders table below to that month

## Hidden features — behaviour beyond the stated change

One acceptance line can carry a feature of its own. A two-step model swap gained a line requiring the drain's per-step tokens line to name model and effort; that line printed neither, so one sentence grew the bead to 40 files. A bead's size must be known at filing, so the operator decides whether an extra is worth its own bead instead of finding it in the diff.

**The stated change** is what the description's **What is wanted** says (for an `ask:`, what the operator asks for). Check every acceptance line against the code at HEAD, once per node, after drafting and before the first `/ac-quality-review` pass. Flag a line only when all three tests hold:

1. **The line requires a behaviour.** Verification evidence of the stated change is not a behaviour: a test that pins it, a gate or suite that passes, a run record, a regenerated doc, a `DECISIONS.md` row. New or changed product output is a behaviour, even when it reports on the stated change: a field added to a log line, a printed line, a column, a flag, an endpoint field. "The tokens line names the model" is a behaviour; "a test pins the formula's model" is not.
2. **The stated change does not include it.** The description does not state that behaviour as wanted, and the stated change works without it. Every feature asks for something that does not exist yet: a line whose new behaviour is the stated change itself is never flagged.
3. **The code at HEAD does not do it.** You read the code (or the repo facts the invoker gave) and it does not do it today; cite the path. A line naming behaviour that already exists at HEAD is never flagged, even when the description never mentions that surface. A line you could not check against the code stands: never flag on wording alone.

For each flagged line there are exactly two ways forward: **reword** the line to the stated change, or **split** the behaviour into its own bead. There is no third way and no override; an author who wants the extra in this bead states it in the description.

- **Args mode, a bead spec** — return one fenced ```json``` block and build no node:

  ```json
  {"error": "hidden_feature",
   "findings": [{
     "line": "<the acceptance line, verbatim>",
     "behaviour": "<what the line requires that does not exist yet>",
     "stated_change": "<the description's stated change, one phrase>",
     "repo_fact": "<path[:line]> — <what the code does today>",
     "ways_forward": {"reword": "<the line cut down to the stated change>",
                      "split": "<title for a bead of its own>"}}]}
  ```

  One `findings` entry per flagged line; `ways_forward` holds exactly `reword` and `split`. The invoker re-sends the spec with the line reworded, or removes it and sends a second spec for the behaviour.
- **Args mode, an `ask:`** — draft no such line. For each behaviour left out, add one line to the node's `notes`: `Left out: <behaviour> — beyond the ask's stated change; <path> <what the code does today>. File it as its own bead if it is wanted.` Return the plan as usual.
- **Interactive mode** — before showing the assembled plan, show each flagged line to the author with its repo fact and the two choices, reword or split. A split becomes its own node in the same plan. File nothing until the author has chosen for every flagged line.

## One bead per ask — split only at a real boundary

File the whole ask as one bead, across every layer it touches. A sequential chain over the same code (struct, then loader, then validator) is one bead: the chain buys no parallelism and pays a review pass per link. Split only where one of these holds, and name the boundary in each node's `notes`:

- **Independent tracks** — two parts share no paths and can land in either order. Each is its own node, with no edge between them.
- **A wide refactor** — the procedure below.
- **An operator decision between halves** — the second half cannot be specified until the operator rules on the first. The first half is a node; the second waits on it with a blocking edge, and its open question goes to the operator.
- **The spend and review budget** — the ask cannot plausibly land inside one bead's spend cap (`.djinn/config.json` `max_cost_usd_per_bead`) and the review loop's 3 attempts (`core/iter.formula.toml` review-loop). Split along the line where each part ships on its own.

Neither size, nor layer, nor line count is a boundary: an ask with backend and frontend halves and a dozen outcomes is one bead. Nodes that share a brief (a wide refactor, a decision between halves, a budget split) go under one epic — the owning open epic, or a new epic node in the same plan whose description carries the shared brief. Independent tracks are separate asks: each goes under the invoker's `parent` or the epic that owns it, never under a new epic made only to group them.

#### Wide refactors — the exception to vertical slicing

One class of work breaks the rule above. A **wide refactor** is a single mechanical change — rename a column, retype a shared symbol, move a package — whose **blast radius** fans across the codebase: one edit breaks call sites in every corner of the tree at once, so no vertical slice can land green and a planner who forces one emits beads that cannot pass their own gate. Recognize it by blast radius, not by size — the change itself is trivial; what makes it wide is how many callers it breaks simultaneously.

Do not force a wide refactor into vertical slices. Sequence it as **expand → migrate → contract**, and wire the phases with real blocking edges in the plan:

1. **Expand** — one bead that adds the new form *beside* the old one, touching no call sites. Nothing breaks, because nothing has moved yet. This bead blocks every bead below it.
2. **Migrate** — call sites move in **batches sized by blast radius** (per package, per directory, per module), and **each batch is its own bead, blocked by the expand bead**. The suite stays green batch to batch because the old form still exists — that is the whole reason to expand first. Batches run in parallel unless two of them touch the same file, where the Step 4 sibling-file check still applies.
3. **Contract** — one bead that deletes the old form once no caller remains, **blocked by every migrate batch**. Miss one of those edges and `bd ready` will surface the delete while a caller still points at the old form.

**Fallback when the batches cannot stay green alone.** Some refactors have no expand form that keeps each batch green in isolation — an exhaustive-match retype, a schema change the ORM validates at boot. Keep the same expand → migrate → contract sequence, but let the migrate batches **share an integration branch** and **all block a final integrate-and-verify bead**. Green is promised only at that integration bead: each batch's acceptance criteria describe its own call-site conversion, and the integrate-and-verify bead carries the suite-green criterion for the whole chain. Say so in the batch beads' `notes` — an executing agent that expects a green suite from its own bead will otherwise thrash against a failure the plan already accounted for.

The sibling-file check: two batches whose `touches` share a file are merged into one batch or ordered by an edge. Wide-refactor beads take structural acceptance lines ("no reference to `old_column` remains under `internal/`") and no UI lines.

### Edges

A blocking edge only where one node cannot land before another: expand before each migrate batch, every batch before contract, a decision before the half that waits on it. Independent tracks get none, and a node's position in the plan never makes one. An edge reads **from the waiting node to the node it waits on**: `{"from_key": "B", "to_key": "A", "type": "blocks"}` keeps B out of `bd ready` until A closes. Non-blocking links ride the same list as `"type": "related"`.

## `touches` — the file-overlap path list

`touches` is the list of paths a bead is expected to change, in the node's `metadata`. The summoner reads it at dispatch: two ready beads whose lists overlap are never worked side by side, and a bead without it is never held, so it can collide with a bead editing the same file. It is **required on every node**; the judgment belongs here, at filing, where the design is in front of the author.

**Shape.** A JSON array of strings. Paths are **repo-relative** — no leading `./`, no absolute paths, no globs. A **directory ends in a trailing slash** (`internal/djinn/drainstate/`) and covers everything beneath it; anything else is one file (`cmd/summoner/spawner.go`):

```json
"metadata": {"touches": ["cmd/summoner/", "internal/djinn/drainstate/"]}
```

**What to list.** The paths the work will edit, at the coarsest honest granularity: the directory when the bead owns the package, the file when it touches one corner of a shared one. **When unsure, take the directory**: a lost parallel slot is cheaper than a lost worktree. Never emit an empty array: "this bead overlaps nothing" is a claim no bead that changes the repo can make.

**Never `CONTEXT_MAP.md`.** Workers never edit the root `CONTEXT_MAP.md` (work contract §7): the gardener seat maintains it, and a landing that changes it is deferred. A `touches` entry equal to `CONTEXT_MAP.md` — the exact root path, nothing else — plans a change no worker may make. In args mode, return a structured error naming the entry and contract §7 (route the map change to the gardener seat as a duty) and build no node. In interactive mode, drop the entry, say why, and file the rest. Only the exact entry triggers this: `docs/CONTEXT_MAP.md` is an ordinary file, and a description that mentions `CONTEXT_MAP.md` is no reason to refuse.

**Never `.djinn/seats/`.** Workers never edit a seat's files (work contract §7; `docs/adr/2026-09-28-seat-run-commits-seat-files.md`): only `djinn seat run` writes them, and a landing that changes one is deferred. A `touches` entry equal to `.djinn/seats/` or beginning with it plans a change no worker may make; its owning seat is the path segment after `.djinn/seats/` (`.djinn/seats/lead/duties.toml` belongs to `lead`). In args mode, return a structured error naming the entry, the owning seat and contract §7, citing that ADR, and build no node; name every such entry when there are several. In interactive mode, drop the entry, say why, and file the rest. Route the change to that seat as a duty, or to the lead for an attended landing on main; for a shipped seat the drain path is its template under `internal/djinn/seat/templates/` — list `internal/djinn/seat/templates/<seat>/` in `touches`, and the change reaches `.djinn/seats/<seat>/` through `djinn init --resync-seats`. Only a `touches` entry with that exact prefix triggers this: `.djinn/seatsx/`, `docs/.djinn/seats/x`, `.djinn/lead/file.md`, `internal/djinn/seat/templates/lead/duties.toml` and a `.djinn/` directory entry are ordinary paths, and a description that mentions a seat file is no reason to refuse.

## `ac_labels` — a name per criterion

`ac_labels` names each acceptance criterion in a few words. The ops room's bead detail lists a bead's criteria in a narrow column, one row each, with a status tick; a criterion's own text is a sentence that does not fit there. The label is that row. The acceptance text itself is untouched: the AC gate, the evidence writer and verify-acceptance read only `acceptance_criteria`.

**Shape.** A JSON array of strings under `metadata.ac_labels`, aligned by position with the non-blank `acceptance_criteria` lines: label *i* names line *i*, and the array is exactly as long as the non-blank line count.

**Who writes it.** Args mode takes an optional `ac_labels` list. Absent, the skill authors one label per criterion, in args and interactive mode alike, so every node carries the key. Author the labels from the acceptance text the gate approved, after the gate: a tightening pass rewrites lines. Passed labels keep their lines when the gate left the line count unchanged; when tightening changed the count, author the whole list again.

**The authoring rule.** Each label is a noun phrase of 2 to 6 words naming the criterion's outcome — what is true when the line holds, not how it is checked — at most 32 cells, distinct within the bead. It opens on the thing the line is about (a noun), never on a verb or participle: `Narrow ruling line cut short`, not `Cut to width, never wrapped`. It contains none of `Given`, `→`, `pinned`, `verified`, a test name (a word beginning with a capital `Test`, such as `TestDetailLogDigest`), the word `test` or `tests` in any case (a gate line names the suite: `Fast suite and audit green`), a path (no `/`) or a file:line. Good: `Header: state, id, priority, round`; `401 on expired tokens`; `Fast suite and audit green`. Not `Given a bead → the row reads x` (a sentence), not `TestDetailLogDigest passes` (how it is checked), not `ops/cockpit.go reads labels` (a path).

**Wrong length.** In args mode, an `ac_labels` list whose length differs from the non-blank acceptance line count returns a structured error naming both counts (`ac_labels has 3 labels; acceptance has 4 non-blank lines`) and builds no node: guessing which label belongs to which line would put a wrong name on a criterion. The error proposes no label and no corrected list, not even as a hint: the invoker re-sends a list of the right length, or omits `ac_labels`. In interactive mode, say both counts and author the list again.

## `short_name` — the bead's name in narrow columns

`short_name` is the bead's name wherever a whole title does not fit: the ops room lists beads in narrow columns, and a title cut mid-word reads as noise. The room shows the one this skill wrote; the title itself is untouched.

**Shape.** A JSON string under `metadata.short_name`: at most 28 cells, made of whole words of plain prose, with no `…`, no trailing punctuation (no `.`, `,`, `:`, `;`, `-` or `—` at the end), no line break and no leading or trailing space. A cell is one terminal column: each ASCII character is one cell, a wide character (CJK, emoji) two. Every node carries the key.

**Who writes it.** Args mode takes an optional `short_name` string. A passed value is checked against the rules here and, when it holds, carried unchanged — never shortened, reworded or "improved". Absent, the skill authors one from the title, in args and interactive mode alike.

**The authoring rule.** When the whole title fits in 28 cells, the title is the name (minus any trailing punctuation). Otherwise name what the bead is about in a noun phrase of whole words that fits: the title's leading words, cut only at a space, when they read as a phrase on their own; a fresh phrase from the title's own words when they do not. Never end on a dangling article, preposition or conjunction (`a`, `the`, `with`, `and`), never cut inside a word, never mark the cut with `…`. Good: `JWT validation middleware` for "Add JWT validation middleware" (29 cells); `Short names at filing` for "Every bead files with a short name the skill writes". Not `Every bead files with a` (dangling article), not `Every bead files with a sho` (cut inside a word), not `Every bead files with a…` (an ellipsis).

**A bad passed value.** In args mode, refuse a passed `short_name` that is empty, is over 28 cells, carries `…` or trailing punctuation, or is a prefix of the title that ends inside one of the title's words (the title's next character after the prefix is a letter or digit, not a space). Return a structured error naming the value and its fault — its cell count and the 28-cell limit, or the word it cuts (`"Every bead files with a short na" cuts the title's word "name"`) — and build no node. Before refusing on length, count the value's cells word by word, each word's apostrophe included, then add one per space: `Keep the user's draft intact` is 4 + 3 + 6 + 5 + 6 = 24, plus 4 spaces, = 28 cells, and valid. Refuse on length only a value that count puts over 28. Name every fault the value has. The error proposes no replacement name, not even as a hint: the invoker re-sends a valid name, or omits `short_name`. A value of at most 28 cells that ends at a word boundary of the title is valid even when the title's next word would not fit: carry it unchanged. In interactive mode, say what is wrong and author the name again.

## `agent` — who does the agent work

`agent` names the adapter, model and effort that run a bead's agent steps, on whatever formula the bead runs; it beats the formula's own per-step pins. It is the operator's call: set it only when the operator named the agent. Operators say it as `agent: <adapter> <model> <effort>` — e.g. `agent: codex gpt-6-astra high`.

**Bead-wide form** — overrides every agent step:

```json
"metadata": {"agent": {"adapter": "codex", "model": "gpt-6-astra", "effort": "high"}}
```

**Per-step form** — `agent.steps.<step-id>` overrides one step and beats the bead-wide form on that step:

```json
"metadata": {"agent": {"adapter": "codex", "model": "gpt-6-astra", "effort": "high",
  "steps": {"review": {"adapter": "claude-code", "model": "opus[1m]", "effort": "high"}}}}
```

`steps` may appear without the bead-wide keys; unnamed steps then keep the formula's pins. Every selection names all three knobs. Valid values are the adapter's own: `claude-code` models `opus[1m]`, `opus`, `sonnet[1m]`, `sonnet`, `haiku`, `fable` and the full `claude-*` ids, efforts `low|medium|high|xhigh|max`; `codex` models `gpt-6-astra`, `gpt-6-sol`, `gpt-6-luna`, `gpt-6.1-sol`, efforts `none|minimal|low|medium|high|xhigh|max`. A step id names an agent step of the bead's formula (default: `implement`, `fix-review`, `review`, `fix-regression`; crucible: `try`, `review`, `fix-regression`). An invalid override defers the bead `needs-operator` before any step runs.

## `crucible` — a bead that moves a number

Use it when the operator wants a number a script can measure to get better — slow tests faster, a binary smaller — rather than a done-state. Label the bead `formula:crucible`: an agent makes one change per try, the harness measures it, keeps a real gain, resets the rest, and stops at the target, after `flat` tries in a row are not kept, or at the dollar cap. The kept chain then gets one review pass whose findings are filed as follow-up beads, then the regression loop; if anything committed past the last kept try, the harness re-measures the final tree and lands it only if it still beats the baseline by more than the baseline spread.

**The interview.** Ask the operator only these four, in order:

1. **What number?** — what is being measured, in their words ("slow-tier wall time").
2. **Which direction?** — `lower` or `higher` is better.
3. **Target** — the value that means done, or `none`.
4. **Budget** — the dollar cap on the tries. Required: nothing else bounds the loop. The steps after the loop add to the run's spend.

**Draft the rest from the repo**, then show the whole spec back for confirmation:

- `measure` — the command whose LAST stdout line is the number. Find an existing script and run it once to confirm the last line parses as a number. When none exists, file a blocker bead that writes it, and block this bead on it.
- `runs` — how many times each measurement runs; the score is the median. Default `3`.
- `protect` — every path a try could edit to move the number without improving the thing: the measure script, the fixtures it reads, the guard's config. An entry may be a glob (`**` crosses directories): `**/*_test.go` makes every test file read-only. A glob covers its whole match set — adding or deleting a matching file is a violation too.
- `guard` — the command every try must keep green, e.g. `go test -short ./...`.
- `touches` — the code the improvement may change. The guard enforces it as an allowlist: a try whose diff changes any path outside it is rejected unmeasured. No literal `protect` path may sit inside it; a protect glob may match inside it.
- `stop.flat` — consecutive non-kept tries before giving up. Default `5`.

**Shape.** `crucible {measure, better, runs, protect, guard, stop {target, flat, usd}}` in `metadata`, beside `touches`. `measure` and `stop.usd` are required: a bead missing either defers `needs-operator` at claim. Omit `stop.target` for no target.

**Acceptance criteria** name the number and its record, e.g. `The kept chain lands with the slow-tier median at or below 120 s, with one row per try in .djinn/crucible/<bead-id>.tsv on the branch and the bead's djinn-crucible summary comment reading baseline and best`.

Worked example — "make the slow tier faster, under 120 seconds, $25":

```json
"labels": ["formula:crucible"],
"metadata": {"touches": ["internal/", "cmd/"],
  "crucible": {"measure": "scripts/bench-slow.sh", "better": "lower", "runs": 3,
               "protect": ["scripts/bench-slow.sh", "**/*_test.go"],
               "guard": "go test -short ./...",
               "stop": {"target": 120, "flat": 5, "usd": 25}}}
```

## Field mapping — bead field to plan key

A plan is `{"commit_message": ..., "nodes": [...], "edges": [...]}`. bd drops an unknown key with only a warning — `acceptance` is NOT a plan key, and a node carrying it files a bead with no acceptance criteria.

| Bead field (args key) | Plan key | Shape |
|---|---|---|
| title | `title` | string |
| type | `type` | `epic` / `feature` / `task` / `chore` / `bug` |
| priority | `priority` | integer 0-4 |
| description | `description` | string (markdown) |
| design | `design` | string (markdown); omit when absent |
| acceptance | `acceptance_criteria` | string, one criterion per line |
| notes | `notes` | string (markdown); omit when absent |
| labels | `labels` | array of strings |
| touches | `metadata.touches` | `"metadata": {"touches": [...]}`; always present, never empty |
| ac_labels | `metadata.ac_labels` | beside `touches`; always present, one string per non-blank `acceptance_criteria` line |
| short_name | `metadata.short_name` | beside `touches` and `ac_labels`; always present |
| agent | `metadata.agent` | beside `touches`; omit when absent |
| crucible | `metadata.crucible` | beside `touches`; only with the `formula:crucible` label |
| key | `key` | plan-local node key, unique in the plan |
| parent in the same plan | `parent_key` | the parent node's `key` |
| parent that already exists | `parent_id` | the existing bead id |
| blocked by a node in the same plan | edge `from_key` / `to_key` | `{"from_key": <blocked>, "to_key": <blocker>, "type": "blocks"}` |
| blocked by an existing bead | edge `from_key` / `to_id` | `{"from_key": <blocked>, "to_id": <blocker id>, "type": "blocks"}` |

A lone bead is a one-node plan:

```json
{
  "commit_message": "file: Expired sessions sign the user out cleanly",
  "nodes": [
    {
      "key": "bead",
      "title": "Expired sessions sign the user out cleanly",
      "type": "feature",
      "priority": 2,
      "description": "**What is wanted:** ...",
      "acceptance_criteria": "Given an expired token on any protected route → 401 with error code session_expired\nGiven a 401 session_expired in the app → the sign-in page opens with the user's unsaved draft still in the editor after sign-in",
      "design": "Tokens are issued in internal/auth/; the app's request layer is web/src/lib/api/.",
      "notes": "Source: docs/auth-design.md §Expiry",
      "labels": ["auth"],
      "metadata": {"touches": ["internal/auth/", "web/src/lib/api/"],
                   "ac_labels": ["401 on an expired session", "Draft kept across sign-in"],
                   "short_name": "Clean session expiry"},
      "parent_id": "djinn-auth1"
    }
  ],
  "edges": [
    {"from_key": "bead", "to_id": "djinn-abc12", "type": "blocks"}
  ]
}
```

## Internal AC-quality gate — iteration budget

The hidden-feature check (Hidden features, above) runs first, once per node; the gate sees only a draft that passed it. Before filing, run `/ac-quality-review` on each node's drafted `acceptance_criteria`, passing the draft text, its `description` and its `type`. This is the only place the gate runs: the bead-work contract (§2) settles acceptance-criteria quality at filing.

<!-- djinn-dispatch: claude-code -->
**Invoking the gate:** run `/ac-quality-review` through the Skill tool, in this conversation.
<!-- djinn-dispatch: end -->

**A CONCRETE verdict does not end this skill.** `/ac-quality-review` returns a verdict and hands control back. In the same turn, continue to the `bd create --graph` call (Filing) and report the new bead id(s) — or, without `--execute`, return the gate-approved plan. A run that stops at the verdict has filed nothing.

**Iteration protocol** — a 2-iteration tightening budget, so at most 3 review passes per node:

1. Invoke `/ac-quality-review` with the draft.
2. **CONCRETE with an empty `operator_required[]`** → the node is approved.
3. **UNDERSPEC, or a non-empty `operator_required[]`** → apply each `findings[i].rewrite_hint` to its line, reword each `operator_required[i].criterion` (below), keep unflagged lines in order, and invoke the gate again. At most twice.
4. **Still UNDERSPEC on the third pass** → **HALT.** Do NOT emit `bd create`. Return the third pass's `findings[]` as an actionable error naming each line's `minimum_output` and `rewrite_hint`: the intent is not clear enough yet to state as outcomes, and a person decides whether to restate the ask.

**`operator_required[]` is the second half of the gate.** A non-empty `operator_required[]` is handled exactly like `UNDERSPEC`: reword the flagged line so the unattended harness can satisfy it — drop the interactive step, replace an external action with the observable it would produce, or split the human part into its own separately filed bead — inside the SAME 2-iteration tightening budget. If `operator_required[]` is still non-empty on the third pass, **HALT**: do NOT emit `bd create`. Surface its entries the same way, naming each `manual_step`. Filing time is where this is decided because no drain step re-checks an operator-required criterion: a bead filed with one spends implementation iterations on work no unattended agent can finish.

One HALT holds the whole plan: file nothing until every node is approved.

## Drafting in a helper

A caller that must keep its own context lean — the lead on a long source document, a seat — may hand the whole ask to the djinn-planner agent `djinn init` writes. The helper runs this skill without `--execute` and returns only the gate-approved plan or `{HALT, findings[]}`; it never files, and the caller files the plan it returns. When the agent file is missing, run `djinn init --resync` (in a home realm, `djinn skills install --global`) first.

<!-- djinn-dispatch: claude-code -->
**Starting the helper:** use the Agent tool with `subagent_type: djinn-planner` (`.claude/agents/djinn-planner.md`, else `~/.claude/agents/djinn-planner.md`) and **`model: fable`**, passing the ask verbatim.
<!-- djinn-dispatch: end -->

## Filing — one `bd create --graph` call

Filing runs only after every node is approved by the gate and the bd 1.3.0 preflight passed.

1. **Resolve every existing id.** For each `parent` and `blocked_by` id, run `bd show <id> --json`. Stop if any is missing: bd accepts a `parent_id` or `to_id` that names no bead, and a dangling blocker edge leaves the bead ready.
2. **Stage every field in a per-invocation scratch dir** and assemble the plan with `jq --rawfile` (the quoting gotcha) — never hand-write multi-line markdown into a JSON string, and never retype an approved line.
3. **Pre-filing check** — only when a node carries the `proposed` label (below).
4. **Dry-run.** `bd create --graph "$d/plan.json" --dry-run --json`. Stop on any error or any `unknown field(s)` warning.
5. **File.** `bd create --graph "$d/plan.json" --json` returns `{"ids": {"<key>": "<new-id>"}}`. Whole plan or nothing: on an error no bead was created, so fix the plan and re-run — never file the nodes one at a time.
6. **Read back** (Post-filing verification).

```bash
d="$(mktemp -d)"
cat > "$d/description.md" <<'EOF'
**What is wanted:** ...
EOF
cat > "$d/acceptance.txt" <<'EOF'
Given an expired token on any protected route → 401 with error code session_expired
EOF
jq -n --rawfile description "$d/description.md" --rawfile acceptance "$d/acceptance.txt" \
  'def t: rtrimstr("\n");
   {commit_message: "file: Expired sessions sign the user out cleanly",
    nodes: [{key: "bead", title: "Expired sessions sign the user out cleanly", type: "feature", priority: 2,
             description: ($description|t), acceptance_criteria: ($acceptance|t), labels: ["auth"],
             metadata: {touches: ["internal/auth/", "web/src/lib/api/"],
                        ac_labels: ["401 on an expired session"], short_name: "Clean session expiry"},
             parent_id: "djinn-auth1"}],
    edges: [{from_key: "bead", to_id: "djinn-abc12", type: "blocks"}]}' > "$d/plan.json"
bd create --graph "$d/plan.json" --dry-run --json   # stop on any error or unknown-field warning
bd create --graph "$d/plan.json" --json             # → {"ids": {"bead": "<new-id>"}}
```

### Pre-filing check — proposed plans only

When any node's labels hold `proposed` (seat-originated work), ask a judge of the other model family whether the plan is worth building before it is filed, so its objections arrive while fixing them is still an edit. With no `proposed` label, skip it and record nothing. It runs once per plan and never blocks filing.

<!-- djinn-dispatch: claude-code -->
The judge is astra: pass `--only astra`.
<!-- djinn-dispatch: end -->

```bash
djinn triage preview --plan "$d/plan.json" --only <judge> --json > "$d/prefile.json"
# → [{"key": "<top-level key>", "votes": [{"vote": "go|no-go|abstain", "hard_rule": null|"<name>", "reason": "<one sentence>"}]}]
```

Each top-level node (no `parent_key`) gets one vote; append one `prefile:` line to that node's `notes`, then take one branch:

- **`no-go`, or a non-null `hard_rule`** — fix each finding you agree with; a changed node goes back through the gate. For each finding you reject, append `prefile rejected: <finding> — <why>`. Then append `prefile: <judge> <vote>[ [<hard-rule>]] — <reason>; fixed <n>, rejected <m>`. Do not run the preview again.
- **`go`** — append `prefile: <judge> go — <reason>`.
- **`abstain`, or a non-zero exit** — append `prefile: unavailable — <reason>`.

Rebuild `plan.json` from the staged files so the `prefile:` lines reach the plan, then continue to the dry-run.

## Gotcha: multiline quoting

Write each multi-line field to a file with a quoted heredoc (`<<'EOF'`) and read it into the plan with `jq --rawfile`, which does all JSON escaping. Heredoc-in-`$(...)` breaks on `[[` patterns and apostrophes, and hand-escaped JSON breaks on the first stray quote. Stage under `mktemp -d`, never fixed `/tmp/bead-*` names: concurrent invocations would clobber each other's fields.

## Output

### Args mode

- **Without `--execute`**: file nothing. Return the gate-approved plan as one fenced ```json``` block, `{"nodes": [...], "edges": [...]}` — each node exactly as the Field mapping builds it (`key`, every present field, `acceptance_criteria` as the gate approved it, `metadata.touches`, `metadata.ac_labels` and `metadata.short_name` always), and an edge for every `blocked_by` id and every boundary edge. Most asks return one node and no edges besides its blockers.
- **With `--execute`**: file the plan (Filing), run the post-filing verification, and return `{bead_ids, short_names}`.
- **On HALT or a structured error**: one fenced ```json``` block with the error (the third pass's `findings[]`, the missing keys, the refused value and its fault, or a `hidden_feature` finding); build no node and file nothing.

### Interactive mode

Show the assembled plan for review. When the ask split into more than one node, show each node's title and the boundary that split it, and wait for a yes: the plan's shape is the operator's call. File it, run the post-filing verification, then report each new bead id with its title.

### Post-filing verification — every returned id

For each id in the returned `ids` map, run `bd show <id> --json` and confirm on `.[0]`:

- `acceptance_criteria` is non-empty and equals the gate-approved text.
- `metadata.touches` equals the drafted list.
- `metadata.ac_labels` equals the drafted labels, as many as the non-blank `acceptance_criteria` lines — `bd show <id> --json | jq '.[0].metadata.ac_labels'`.
- `metadata.short_name` equals the drafted name: present, at most 28 cells, whole words — `bd show <id> --json | jq '.[0].metadata.short_name'`.
- `metadata.agent` and `metadata.crucible` equal the drafted values, or are absent when none was drafted.
- `parent` equals the drafted parent, and `dependencies` holds a `dependency_type: "blocks"` entry for every drafted blocker.

Then run `bd ready --exclude-type=epic`: a node that waits on another must not be listed. Fix a wrong field with `bd update <id>`; an `acceptance_criteria` repair passes `/ac-quality-review` before it is written.

## Failure-mode handling

- **bd below 1.3.0** — stop before any filing (Preflight).
- **Missing required key** — args mode: a structured error naming the keys; interactive mode: ask.
- **`ac_labels` of the wrong length, a bad `short_name`, a `touches` entry that is `CONTEXT_MAP.md` or under `.djinn/seats/`** — args mode: the structured error each section names; build no node.
- **An acceptance line requiring behaviour beyond the stated change that HEAD lacks** — args mode, a spec: the `hidden_feature` finding, no node; an `ask:`: leave the line out with a `Left out:` note; interactive mode: the author picks reword or split before the plan is shown (Hidden features).
- **Parent epic unclear** — run `bd list --type=epic --status=open --no-parent`; ask which one owns the ask, or file a new epic node in the same plan with the bead's `parent_key` pointing at it.
- **Existing id not found** — stop filing; ask, or return the error.
- **`/ac-quality-review` or `bd` unavailable** — surface the error. Never file without the gate.

## Universal constraints

- **Read-only on existing beads.** Tightening happens on the draft, before filing.
- **No silent fields.** An optional field the invoker omits stays omitted; never invent design notes, priorities or paths.
